The person's Discord account and servers, and installing a bot in a server.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Discord account in the Gateway, once, and every app that asks uses it. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

The redirect URI to register, with your Gateway's address (like `apps.example.com`):

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/discord/callback
```

Posting as the bot uses the bot's own token, an app secret the Gateway doesn't hold. Not yet tried against a live connect.

1. Open [discord.com](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and create an OAuth app (also called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and client secret. The secret is often shown only once.

Add it to your Gateway. It asks for the client ID and secret:

```bash
everyapp provider add discord
```

Or add it in **Manage workspace → Providers**.

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  discord: { access: "read", scopes: ["servers.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

Apps ask for these scope sets:

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Discord account (who you are) | `identify` |
| `servers.read` | Servers you are in (read) | `identify`, `guilds` |
| `bot.write` | Add the bot to a server | `identify`, `guilds`, `bot` |

**Check it worked:** `everyapp provider show discord` shows the client as set. Then open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Discord**.

Something wrong or missing? [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Discord).
